subject: Committed spend — staggered replenishment & burn allocation
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudmetrics.io>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@cloudmetrics.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Committed spend — exploring staggered replenishment options

Rishi,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: we (CloudMetrics) are evaluating a 3-year committed spend with Redwood and want a structure that aligns seasonally with our product launches. Our finance and procurement teams prefer a prepay wallet model but want the ability to stagger drawdowns (so we don't front-load cash need) and to include clear top-up triggers rather than constant manual replenishments.

High-level ask: can Redwood propose a few practical drawdown templates (staircase, quarterly buckets with auto-top-ups, and a flat monthly burn-down) and the term discount implications for each? We submitted a rough usage forecast attached.

Also: procurement will ask for PO vs invoice flow, SOC2 evidence, and a sample term sheet to speed legal review.

Attachments: CloudMetrics-3yr-usage-forecast.xlsx (spread of expected tokens/month, pro forma)

Would like to get a proposal before our finance committee on June 24 — could we sync next week?

Thanks,
Ethan Cole
CFO, CloudMetrics
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudmetrics.io>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@cloudmetrics.io>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed spend — exploring staggered replenishment options

Ethan — appreciate the forecast, that helps a lot. I put together three practical structures and attached a draft term sheet for legal to glance at. High-level options below — happy to walk through on a quick call.

Option 1 — Laddered wallet (recommended for seasonality)
- 3-year prepay split into annual buckets (Year1/Year2/Year3) with optional quarterly sub-buckets.
- Discount scale: 7% off list if annualization only; +3% step-up if customer commits to quarterly top-ups and 12-month minimum usage ramp.
- Auto top-up trigger: when a monthly bucket consumes >85% of remaining credits, Redwood will execute a buffered top-up from a reserved tranche to avoid service interruption.

Option 2 — Quarterly replenishment with true-up
- Prepay funds deposited to a central wallet; monthly burn reduces the wallet; quarterly reconciliations and top-ups to maintain headroom.
- Discount: 6% base, with additional volume tiers that increase discount to 10% at defined spend thresholds.

Option 3 — Flat prepay + monthly drawdown
- One-time larger prepay with monthly burn-down and annual true-up. Cleaner for accounting but higher up-front cash.
- Discount: up to 8% depending on total committed amount and payment terms.

Other notes:
- Pilot period: we can offer a 6-month pilot with higher overage caps (10–15% buffer) and a single true-up to validate baseline consumption before the full laddered schedule begins.
- Billing: support PO-driven invoicing or standard Net30 invoicing.
- Compliance: attaching draft term sheet and will include SOC2 + data flow diagrams on request.

Attachment: redwood-draft-term-sheet-v1.pdf

Can we block 30 minutes Thursday morning (6/17) to go over the numbers? If those time windows don't work, send preferred slots.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudmetrics.io>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed spend — exploring staggered replenishment options (numbers)

Ethan — quick follow with real numbers so your finance team has something concrete. Using your forecast, here are three sample envelopes (net of discount):

1) Laddered (recommended) — 3-yr commit = $1.8M total
   - Year 1: $540k (30%) — Quarterly buckets (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4) with an 85% auto-top-up threshold
   - Year 2: $630k (35%) — higher discount tier kicks in at $500k annual usage
   - Year 3: $630k (35%) — step-up discount applies; rollover of unused credits allowed up to 10% cap
   - Effective blended discount: ~10.5% over list with PO + annual prepay on Year1 and automatic quarterly reconciliation

2) Quarterly replenishment + true-up — 3-yr commit = $1.75M
   - Lower upfront: $200k deposit, quarterly top-ups as consumption demands
   - Effective blended discount: ~8% with volume bonuses at $600k+ annual burn

3) Flat prepay — 3-yr commit = $1.85M
   - One-time payment; highest discount applied upfront (12%) but cashflow impact is significant

I attached a CSV with the month-by-month burn projections (redwood-proposal-numbers.csv). We can flip the ladder percentages to match any specific revenue recognition needs if finance requires escrow-style schedules.

Call: https://calendly.com/redwood/aditya-30min — I can take the numbers and walk your FP&A through the logic.

—Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudmetrics.io>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@cloudmetrics.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed spend — exploring staggered replenishment options (numbers)

Thanks Aditya — that helps a lot. CloudMetrics' FB/ML release cadence means Year1 consumption will be lumpy, so the laddered approach looks promising. Two asks from procurement and finance before we can sign: 

1) Early overage cap: we need a 12% buffer for the first 6 months (instead of the 10% you mentioned) because of our launch schedule. Will Redwood absorb the first 6% of overage and invoice the additional 6% at a reduced overage rate?
2) Auto-top-up mechanics: when the monthly bucket hits 85%, we want an opt-in for an automatic replenish from a reserved tranche, but we also want the ability to disable it at the account level for any quarter if needed. Please spell out the rollback and notification flow.
3) Procurement: we will issue a PO; legal wants a sample SOW + SOC2 attestation and a data flow diagram for any customer-side KV caching or token logs.

Attaching procurement-checklist.pdf with their standard asks. If we can get DocuSign-ready term sheet, our committee can approve on June 24.

Attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf

Best,
Ethan
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudmetrics.io>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@redwood.ai, finance@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed spend — staggered replenishment & next steps

Ethan / team — looping in legal and finance to close out procurement items. Quick confirms from our side: 

- Early overage: we can absorb the first 6% of overage for the first 6 months. Any overage beyond that will be invoiced at a pre-agreed reduced overage rate (we propose 60% of list overage for the first true-up).
- Auto-top-up: implemented as an account-level setting. Default = ON. When a monthly bucket reaches 85% remaining, an automated top-up from a reserved tranche will create a 10% buffer and send an email + webhook to your procurement inbox. You can opt out per quarter via the console or by sending the opt-out flag to support. Rollback: top-ups can be disabled for future buckets but cannot retroactively withdraw applied credits.
- Billing: we support PO-based invoicing; standard payment terms Net30 after PO receipt.
- Compliance: legal will attach SOC2 Type II attestation and a data flow diagram for KV caching/token logs in the next email. We can also produce a redline-friendly DocuSign term sheet (link below) to accelerate execution.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/67890/company/CloudMetrics/opportunity/CM-2027-0073, DocuSign: https://docusign.com/sign/abc123

If that sounds ok, Aditya / Rishi — please produce a final term sheet with the agreed 6% absorb + reduced overage pricing and updated auto-top-up mechanics. Ethan — once we share the DocuSign, you should be able to send PO + sign to hit your finance committee timeline.

Thanks — Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
